title: Prescribe make bootstrap: onboarding as an enforced target, not a runbook walk
description:
**Problem.** `docs/runbooks/adopt-beads.md` is ~300 lines, and every line of it is either an
ordering constraint or a verification obligation — the two things prose cannot enforce. Three
adoptions have each discovered a new way to get it wrong, and each fix added a paragraph asking
the next agent to be more careful. That does not converge.

Adopting beads on shelf produced four defects in one session, each defeating a runbook rule that
was actually followed: `bd init` seizing `core.hooksPath` and killing the commit guard; a
`git reset --hard` silently reverting `bd config set`; beads and the pre-commit framework
contending for one hook slot; and the guard reporting a checkmark while provably dead.

**Shape of a fix.** Stop writing instructions for an agent to follow; prescribe a target the repo
runs. `make bootstrap` is idempotent, encodes ordering as prerequisites, asserts the effects it
intended (never the artifacts it wrote), and reports live / not-live / could-not-check as three
distinct outcomes. `make bootstrap-verify` joins `make check`, so decay fails the build instead
of going unnoticed. The beads runbook keeps every finding but converts its voice from
instructions-to-a-reader into assertions-a-target-makes.

**Trigger:** none needed — this is active work, blocked only on sequencing.

Blocked by shelf-efh: that change produces the first real verify-by-behavior implementation this
one generalizes. Landing the contract first would prescribe a pattern with no working instance,
which is the "do NOT build on spec" the constitution warns against.

Proposal: openspec/changes/bootstrap-target-contract/
Closes shelf-gag if design D4 (make check depends on bootstrap-verify) lands as proposed.

title: Commit guard is silently dead when core.hooksPath is set
description:
**Problem.** `tools/hooks/install.py` writes the guard to `<git-dir>/hooks/pre-commit`, a
hardcoded path (line 52: `hooks = git_dir / "hooks"`). It never consults
`git config core.hooksPath`. When a repo sets `core.hooksPath`, git stops reading
`.git/hooks` entirely — so the installer reports success, the file exists, and the guard
never fires.

**Evidence (verified 2026-08-12, this repo, not inferred).** `bd init` sets
`core.hooksPath = .beads/hooks`. A probe hook written to `.git/hooks/pre-commit` containing
`exit 1` did **not** block a commit — the commit succeeded cleanly. The `.beads/hooks/*`
shims contain only bd's own marker-delimited block; they do not chain through to any
pre-existing hook.

**Scope is wider than beads.** `husky`, `lefthook`, and the `pre-commit` framework all set
`core.hooksPath` the same way. Any consumer using any of them has a silently-dead shelf
guard today.

**Relationship to the per-clone gap:** distinct. That one is "unarmed until you run the
installer". This one is "disarmed *even after* you run it" — strictly worse, because the
installer's success message makes it look armed.

**Shape of a fix:** resolve the hook directory as
`git rev-parse --git-path hooks` (which honors `core.hooksPath`) instead of
`git_dir / "hooks"`. If the resolved directory is foreign-managed (a beads/husky/lefthook
shim already present), the existing "refuses to clobber a foreign one" branch should either
chain the guard in or fail loudly — deciding which is part of this issue.

Found while adopting beads on shelf (docs/runbooks/adopt-beads.md); the runbook needs this
recorded as a Phase 1 gap.

title: Verify convert-md's HTML render path against a real web corpus (BENCH)
description:
The docx work (docx-engine-verification, design.md D7) established that `convert_html`'s
`web_page` kind uses trafilatura (extraction) and `clean` uses html2text (faithful render).
Only html2text's clean path is now exercised widely (via docx).

**Unverified:** whether trafilatura is the *best* web extractor, and whether html2text vs
markdownify is the *right* canonical clean renderer. Untested on a real web corpus — and it
touches a2web's live path.

**Shape of a fix:** a `WORKFLOW: BENCH` run (resolution 0011) with a real-web corpus is the
proper treatment.

**Trigger:** build when it matters.

— pandoc dropped for mammoth.

title: Guard enforcement is per-clone — a fresh clone is unguarded
description:
Onboarding installs the hook in one command (`tools/hooks/install.py`,
docs/consuming-the-shelf.md §2), but git hooks can't be committed, so a fresh clone is
unguarded until someone runs it.

**Trigger:** a 2nd machine/clone, OR the first leaked override — then fold a working-tree
check into `make check` (or enforce in CI).

title: a2web adopts anyllm.ProviderName (decided direction, unbuilt)
description:
`anyllm-v0.3.0` (ledger 0037) added a `StrEnum` on the shelf side; a2web's plugin-registry
keys (`"anthropic"`, `"claude-code"`) and `ProviderMode` Literal (`settings.py:30`) are a
*different* string set — not cosmetic drift, so this isn't a mechanical rename.

**Decided 2026-07-09: adopt, not just align** — that's the only way to get drift-safety on
future anyllm releases. Reasoning, for the a2web session that picks this up:

- Bumping anyllm's pin alone can't force a2web to notice a new provider —
  `build_adapter(provider: str, ...)` stays loosely typed *on purpose* (it's a
  config-ingestion boundary; YAML/env are always strings, so `ty` can't help there, and the
  function already validates at runtime). Static drift-detection has to live in the
  *consumer's* typed code, not the library's boundary function.
- The fix: a2web parses its config string into `ProviderName` **once**, at the settings field
  itself — `ProviderMode = Literal[...]` → `provider: ProviderName` on the
  `pydantic_settings.BaseSettings` field. `StrEnum` is natively a pydantic validator; no
  custom `field_validator` needed. Everything downstream in a2web becomes `ProviderName`-typed
  for free.
- Payoff: an exhaustive `match`/`case` (`assert_never` on the fallback, no wildcard) anywhere
  downstream then gets `ty`-checked — a future anyllm provider added without a matching a2web
  branch fails typecheck on `make check`, not silently at runtime.
- The one real design decision buried in the rename: a2web's plugin registry currently has
  **one** `"claude-code"` plugin where anyllm distinguishes `CLAUDE_CODE_CLI` vs
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SDK` — decide whether a2web wants both exposed as separate plugins or
  deliberately collapses them, don't let the rename paper over that.
- `PluginManifest.name` is a public lookup key (`registry["anthropic"]`) — ships as a breaking
  change, per `RECEIVE` step 4 ("migrate to the new idiom, not the smallest diff... delete
  compat shims").

**Note:** the work itself lands in the a2web repo, not shelf. Tracked here because shelf owns
the `anyllm` side of the contract.

Migrated from docs/backlog.md § "Decide — open forks (a decision, not a build)".
